title: Multi-format ingress bridge with correlation enrichment and tenant-aware routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Replace multiple duplicative ingest shims with a single "bridge" service that accepts JSONL/JSON/compact binary logs, normalizes structured fields, ensures correlation ID propagation (trace_id, span_id, request_id), enriches with tenant mapping and region tags, and routes to downstream sinks (Loki primary, archived S3, and an async ELK adapter).

Why: Current fleet has 4 different ingest adapters with slightly different field mappings, intermittent loss of correlation headers, and tenant-id drift when proxies rewrite IDs. This causes fractured tracing, missed joins in latency dashboards, and complicated downstream parsing. Consolidating into a single translator reduces maintenance, centralizes enrichment, and enables consistent schema evolution and sampling.

Scope: Implement the translator service, in-process adapters for the three major input encodings, tenant mapping lookup with local cache and fallback to service, header-to-field canonicalization rules, schema version stamping, and a routing rules engine (routing by tenant, region, size, and sampling decision). Provide a backward-compatible passthrough mode and a feature flag for correlation enforcement.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Ingest bridge accepts JSONL, application/json, and our compact binary format and normalizes to our structured-log schema v2.
- 99.9% of incoming events retain a valid correlation id after processing when provided.
- Per-event processing p50 < 12ms, p95 < 50ms for typical 1KB events in test harness.
- Can route the same stream to Loki + S3 archive + ELK adapter with at-least-once semantics.
- Automated tests covering 100+ mapping permutations and a perf harness for 10k eps.
- Canary rollout to 10% of tenants with automatic rollback on error-rate spike > 0.5% or latency SLO breach.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Enrichment: prefer local memcache + async refresh for tenant mapping to avoid per-event RPC overhead. Freshness window 1 minute. This trades slight mapping staleness for throughput.
- Correlation enforcement: two modes: permissive (propagate ID if present) and strict (reject/flag events missing correlation ids). We'll ship permissive initially to avoid customer breakage.
- Schema evolution: each normalized event will include "schema_version" and an optional "original_payload" when a mapping fallback is used (to aid debugging). Storing original payload increases storage cost; enabled only for flagged tenants.
- Routing rules evaluate in order: tenant override -> region affinity -> sampling -> sink mapping. Rule engine must be fast and cache-friendly.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge feature branch behind FF, deploy to staging. Run migration test harness with replay of one week of production telemetry.
2) Canary 10% tenants for 48h; monitor error-rate and traced joins.
3) Expand to 50% for 24h. If stable, flip to 100% and deprecate older adapters after 2 weeks.

Monitoring & observability for this work:
- Grafana panel: ingest-bridge/throughput, p50/p95 latency, correlation-preservation-rate, routing-errors, tenant-cache-hit-rate.
- Trace hooks: instrument per-event spans (ingest.receive -> ingest.normalize -> enrich.lookup -> route.dispatch) with the event correlation id included as tag.
- Alerts: correlation-preservation-rate < 99% for 15m, p95 latency > 150ms for 5m, routing-errors spike > 0.5%.

Testing plan: unit tests for mapping rules, end-to-end with staging Loki and S3, fault injection for tenant service timeouts, and load testing to 15k eps.

Migration notes: Maintain the old adapters concurrently; provide a compatibility shim that rewrites older field names to the new schema. We'll add a periodic reconciliation job that checks sample events in Loki vs. translated events for divergence.

Operational notes: The bridge will be horizontally scalable; each replica keeps a bounded LRU tenant mapping cache and subscribes to a small pubsub channel for invalidations. Replica memory budget must keep per-replica cache < 256MB under normal load.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Accept JSONL/JSON/compact-binary and output structured-log schema v2 consistently.
2) Correlation id preserved when provided (>=99.9%).
3) Perf: p50<12ms, p95<50ms on 1KB events in perf harness.
4) Routes to Loki, S3, ELK adapter with >= once semantics.
5) Canary/rollback automation in place.
design_decision_summary: Local tenant mapping cache with async refresh chosen to optimize latency; permissive correlation mode to reduce customer disruption; include schema_version field and optional original_payload for debugging; routing rules are order-based and cached for speed.
rollout_plan: staging -> canary 10% 48h -> 50% 24h -> 100% then deprecate legacy adapters after 2 weeks. Automated rollback on errors/latency SLO violation.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: ingest-bridge throughput, latency p50/p95, correlation-preservation-rate, tenant-cache-hit-rate, routing-errors. Alerts: correlation-preservation-rate <99% for 15m, p95 latency >150ms for 5m, routing-errors >0.5%.
performance_targets: p50 < 12ms, p95 < 50ms for 1KB events in perf harness; target 15k eps cluster-level capacity for initial fleet sizing.
compatibility_matrix: Inputs: JSONL, application/json, compact-binary. Output: structured-log schema v2. Backward compatibility: compatibility-shim option for legacy field names enabled per-tenant.
